messages:
Marco (Product): Quick sync — several large customers asking for private deployment options. They fall into three asks: VPC control plane (managed but isolated), on-prem packaged bundle, and strict air-gapped installs. We need a clear Q2 priority and minimal launch criteria. Thoughts? @sara @james @nikita

Sara (Eng): +1. We should avoid trying to ship all three at once. Propose MVP ordering: 1) VPC control plane (lowest infra ops) 2) On-prem packaged installer (customers that want host-managed VM/GPU) 3) Airgap (most complex).

Nikita (Solutions): Customer signals: BigBank wants on-prem containerized bundle with KMS integration ASAP. HealthCo prefers VPC control plane with private networking and audit logs. RegulatedCo will need airgap but is willing to be a later pilot. So both VPC and on-prem have real demand; order depends on sales runway.

James (Infra): Technical constraints: VPC control plane = we host control plane in our network but allow customer VPC peering + private endpoints. Requires IAM scoping, per-tenant rate limits, KMS passthrough. On-prem package = installer that spins up control and runtime in customer infra, plus config for HSM/KMS. Airgap = offline installer, signed images, long validation.

Marco (Product): Can we get rough dev effort and risk for each? Need acceptance criteria that we can present to GTM. Example acceptance criteria:```- VPC CP: support per-tenant VPC peering, TLS mTLS, KMS passthrough, 99.9% control-plane uptime SLA on Dedicated customers, documentation + terraform module. - On-prem pack: one-click installer (helm/tar), runtime with GPU support, telemetry opt-out, smoke tests for inference, customer onboarding runbook. - Airgap: signed offline artifact set, documented install checklist, customer acceptance tests, security review passed.```

Sara (Eng): Rough T-shirt estimates: VPC CP = M (6-8 wks core + infra work) if we reuse control-plane primitives; On-prem pack = L (10-12 wks) because packaging, support matrix; Airgap = XL (12-20 wks) due to security & distribution. Risks: KMS/HSM integration and network routing for VPC peering are tricky.

James (Infra): Also, monitoring/observability: on-prem customers will want logs + traces. Must decide if we accept pulling metrics to our hosted console or require local retention only. For regulated customers we need retention controls + SIEM integrations.

Nikita (Solutions): Sales input: recommend targeting VPC CP as the primary offering to close 3 mid-market deals quickly. Offer on-prem packaging as a paid professional services + pilot for BigBank. Reserve airgap for enterprise security engagements. This keeps sales motion moving while we build automation.

Marco (Product): Proposed prioritization for Q2: A) VPC control plane (GA to self-serve for mid-market + dedicated SLA) B) On-prem packaged pilot (one or two paid pilots with solutions support) C) Airgap planning (security workstream + legal). Any objections?

Sara (Eng): No objections. Need a spike for KMS/HSM and a small RFC for per-tenant routing + fallback policy (what happens if peering fails?).

James (Infra): I'll own KMS/HSM spike and draft the logging/retention policy. Will need time with security to list must-have controls for airgap.

Nikita (Solutions): I'll coordinate pilot customers and write the success criteria for the on-prem pilot (SLA, uptime, perf). Also will scope support hours and pricing.

Marco (Product): OK — action items: - @sara create RFC for VPC control plane routing and rollout plan (due EOD Thu) - @james KMS/HSM spike + logging policy draft (due next Tue) - @nikita customer pilot plan + pricing (due next Mon) We'll put this into the Q2 roadmap doc and present to GTM sync on Friday.

deploy-bot: Reminder — roadmap doc updated: https://redwood.internal/roadmaps/private-deploy-q2 (edited) :calendar: 

Sara (Eng): Quick note — for on-prem packaging we should standardize on helm + optional kubeadm baremetal path. Minimizes permutations.

Marco (Product): Agree. Keep airgap interfaces consistent with package format (tar of signed images + installer). We'll revisit exact distribution method after security review.

James (Infra): One more thing: network egress policies for VPC CP — we need a policy for telemetry: default off for regulated customers. I'll add that to the draft.

Marco (Product): Thanks team. I'll queue the roadmap PR and tag @gretchen (sales) and @liyah (security) for visibility. Meeting Friday 10am to finalize. :thumbsup:
